result.headline: The GA reached a test mean of 45.6 (seed group 44.3 ± 1.8) against DQN's 20.5 (20.7 ± 1.1), and the survival bonus left DQN unchanged while one GA seed learned to loop, with 25 of 100 test games ending by starvation.
result.summary:
**GA (genetic algorithm, which evolves networks without gradients):** Seed 0 scored a test mean of 45.58 (median 46, max 86). Its 10 wall, 89 body and 1 starved endings are mostly honest crashes, at 27 steps per apple. The seed group averages 44.28, with seeds 1 and 2 at 45.04 and 42.22. Seed 1 is the warning sign: 25 of its 100 test games ended by starvation, at 44 steps per apple, so it wandered. Training curves rose from 0.09 to 50.5 mean over the last 100 games, and the population mean climbed from 0.08 to 45.5. The curve flattened after about 5 minutes, so the 10-minute budget was close to saturated. The GA ran about 264 million env steps, about 480k steps per second on 5 cores.

**DQN (a gradient-based learner with a replay buffer, which predicts the value of each move):** Test mean 20.54 (seed group 20.72). It ate efficiently, at 8 steps per apple, and its games ended by body (80) or wall (20), never by starvation. Its training mean of 14.9 includes exploration moves, so the test score is the figure to trust. It ran about 2.0 million env steps on one core, about 3.5k steps per second. Those are about 130 times fewer steps than the GA, yet it still learned a sensible policy. Per env step it is far more efficient, while per wall-clock minute the GA is much faster.
result.diagnosis:
The survival bonus is +0.1 per move, against +10 per apple, so one apple equals 100 surviving moves. A snake that circles can collect the bonus without eating. Starvation only ends a game after 100 times its length in moves, and it carries no penalty here (starve is not in this recipe). At length 10 that is 1000 moves, worth 100 reward, the same as ten apples. That is why looping is attractive. For the GA, which selects on total reward, looping paid in seed 1 and the population drifted toward it. Seed 0 barely did (1 starved game), and seed 2 died against walls instead (48 wall endings), so the loophole appears only in some seeds. For DQN, gamma 0.95 looks only about 20 moves ahead, and 0.1 per move is worth about 2 in discounted value. That is too small to drive looping, so DQN behaves the same as in the baseline (20.5 against 21.3).

Comparison caveat: the baseline GA used apple 100 and survival 0.1, with no death penalty. The change in this lesson was therefore larger than the lesson text suggests. Relative to apples, survival is now ten times stronger, and a death penalty was added. The baseline GA scored 51.55 on one seed. The seed group mean is 44.3 (spread ±1.8). That gap of about 7 points is larger than the seed spread, but the baseline has only one seed, so treat it as suggestive rather than settled. No prediction was recorded in the run, so the lesson's written prediction cannot be checked here.
result.learned: A reward is optimised literally: a bonus that pays for surviving can be earned by looping without eating, and whether an agent finds that loophole depends on the seed. Always read how the test games ended, not only the score.

recommendations.title: Penalise starving to stop looping
recommendations.why: Seed 1 looped (25 of 100 test games starved, 44 steps per apple), while seed 0 barely did. If a starvation penalty removes the loophole, looping should disappear across seeds without hurting the honest GA.
recommendations.change: Keep the survival bonus and add a starvation penalty of 30 (starve: 30).
recommendations.prediction: GA starved games fall from 25 (seed 1) and 1 (seed 0) to under 3 per 100 games; GA steps per apple fall toward 25-30; GA test mean stays within 42-47.
recommendations.question: Does a starvation penalty stop the GA from looping on the survival bonus?

recommendations.title: Replace survival bonus with hunger cost
recommendations.why: A per-move cost makes waiting bad, so the loophole closes without a separate starvation rule. Hunger and survival are mutually exclusive, so this is a clean swap.
recommendations.change: Replace the survival bonus with a hunger cost of 0.01 per move.
recommendations.prediction: GA starved games drop to 0-2 per 100; GA steps per apple fall below 30; GA test mean rises to about 46-50, since eating sooner is rewarded.
recommendations.question: Does a per-move cost work better than a per-move bonus for avoiding loops?

ideas.title: Compare agents on score per env step
ideas.what: A dashboard view that plots test score against env steps (log scale) and against wall-clock minutes for all agents on one chart, with seed-group bands.
ideas.why: The GA ran about 264M env steps and DQN about 2M in the same 10 minutes. The current curves mix the two units, making it hard to see that DQN is far more step-efficient while the GA is far faster per minute.
ideas.expected: A learner can read sample efficiency (DQN about 10x better per step at this stage) and speed (GA about 130x more steps per second) in one picture.
